items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names reveal intent (`compile_json_path_final_key`, `HasKeyOrArrayIndex`), and a comment explains why the final key is compiled differently. Formatting matches the surrounding code. A small nit: the subclass sits after `CaseInsensitiveMixin` instead of next to the other HasKey classes.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Adds an overridable hook and reuses `compile_json_path` for the leading path segments. A small subclass handles the internal array-index callers, with no per-backend copies of the path logic. No dead code, and the temporary test file was deleted.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: `json.dumps(str(key_transform))` quotes the key safely and also handles integer keys passed directly. No exceptions are swallowed and there are no magic constants. Hidden tests pass (F2P 2/2, P2P 78/78).

items.name: Array-index semantics kept for isnull / exact=None paths
items.name_zh: isnull / exact=None 路径保留数组下标语义
items.evidence: The change is in the shared `HasKeyLookup.as_sql`, so SQLite, MySQL and Oracle all get it. `KeyTransformIsNull.as_oracle`/`as_sqlite` and `KeyTransformExact.as_oracle` now use `HasKeyOrArrayIndex`, which keeps array-index behaviour. Intermediate segments still go through `compile_json_path`.
